title: Common providers: Sweden
coverage: Complete for the national carriers, the mobile network operators and the largest broadband and business ISPs; open-fibre network owners and the municipal city networks are partial.
missing: The municipal city networks (stadsnät): well over a hundred, only Stokab is listed
Smaller business ISPs and regional broadband providers
AS numbers for Stokab and Open Infra (none confirmed as announced)
Status pages other than the three that answered a check on the read date

sources.name: PTS (Swedish Post and Telecom Authority)
sources.terms: The start page answered; the pages under it, the operator list among them, returned a bot-check page to an automated read, so the register and the terms were not read: nothing is copied.
sources.result: Register not read. It is the authority to consult for operators this pack lacks.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Internet in Sweden
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0. Used to cross-check names only (facts); no text is copied.
sources.result: 0 of 14 names were found on the page (whole-word match; a name under three characters is not counted).

sources.name: Wikipedia: Telecommunications in Sweden
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0. Used to cross-check names only (facts); no text is copied.
sources.result: 2 of 14 names were found on the page (whole-word match; a name under three characters is not counted).

sources.name: Each provider's own public website
sources.terms: Only the address itself is recorded (a fact); no content is copied.
sources.result: 14 of 14 websites and 3 support or status pages answered an automated check; an address that did not answer is left empty.

sources.name: RIPEstat as-overview (RIPE NCC)
sources.terms: The RIPEstat terms forbid redistributing RIPEstat data: nothing is copied. Consulted to confirm, for each AS number, that the registered holder is the named provider.
sources.result: 15 AS numbers confirmed, each announced on the read date; a number registered to the provider but not announced was left out.

sources.name: RIPE NCC list of AS names
sources.terms: Its terms were not read: nothing is copied. Searched by name to find the numbers to confirm.
sources.result: Used to find candidate numbers; each was then confirmed as above.

sources.name: NRO delegated statistics (the regional registries' joint list of assigned AS numbers)
sources.terms: Published by the registries for public use; only which registry holds each AS number is taken (a fact).
sources.result: Every AS number in the pack was found in the list; its registry is recorded beside it.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Com Hem
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0. Used to cross-check a fact only; no text is copied.
sources.result: States that Tele2 bought Com Hem and that the Com Hem brand became Tele2.

providers.name: Telia
providers.notes: Fixed and mobile. Its international backbone is Arelion (international pack).

providers.name: Tele2
providers.notes: Fixed, cable and mobile. Com Hem's cable network took the Tele2 name.

providers.name: Telenor Sverige
providers.notes: Fixed and mobile. AS33885 is the Ownit broadband brand.

providers.name: Bredband2
providers.notes: Broadband over the open city networks, homes and business.

providers.name: GlobalConnect
providers.notes: Nordic fibre group, also in the Denmark and Finland packs. AS12552 was IP-Only's number.

providers.name: Iver
providers.notes: IT and network services for business. AS21195 was DGC's number.

providers.name: Stokab
providers.notes: City of Stockholm's dark-fibre network; wholesale only.

providers.name: Open Infra
providers.notes: Open fibre access network; retail through other providers.

providers.name: Sunet
providers.notes: The national research and education network.
